citation: Project owner, Glessner House version 4 reconstruction brief, 29 September 2026: correct intersecting roofs, courtyard and garden-level openings, continuous copper roof at the inner northeast corner, variable-height ashlar courses, and east-wing chimneys. Follow-up 1 October 2026: rebuild west-wing roof, gables and dormer from northwest/west views; carve the north entrance alcove with left-turn steps and door against HABS floor plans. Later 1 October correction: continuous rear ridge, balanced solid south gable and courtyard eave matching the north range. Follow-up 2 October 2026: correct north windows protruding through the eave; rebuild the whole west elevation to the supplied square-on reconstruction, including stone courses, openings, low rear roof, hood, gutters and turret-to-gable alignment; assess north stone appendage and doors. Follow-up 7 October 2026: remove the recessed cuts beside the courtyard dining tower; connect its copper hip to the north roof with raised tiled slopes and matching ridge adornment. Follow-up 8 October 2026: raise the courtyard dining-tower upper glazing to align with the north-wing upper windows, shortening the copper cap while retaining period-appropriate sash divisions. Follow-up 9 October 2026 UTC: correct the front west gable angle and rear section width against the supplied west and northwest images, then validate against both photographs before merging to dev. Later 9 October correction: restore the west wing's full-height level ridge, simple front and rear gables, and matching courtyard awning; the lowered rear roof and exposed courtyard wall are a regression.
describes_date: 1904-07-01, with modern surviving fabric supplied as qualitative cross-checks
repository: Owner instruction in the project conversation; concise scope and reference inventory retained in docs/RESEARCH/glessner_house_v4.md.
rights_note: The owner supplied the written reconstruction specification and reference images for this implementation. This clearance covers the owner brief; it does NOT claim a reusable licence for the accompanying third-party photographs or Google Earth screenshots. Visible architectural facts and arrangements inform declared reconstruction; no screenshot pixels, photographic textures or photogrammetric meshes are copied.
access_notes: Read in the project conversation on 2026-09-29. Fourteen supplied reference images were also viewed as qualitative comparisons; HABS supplies measured coordinates. Ten additional images supplied and viewed on 2026-10-01 (210139 through 212524). HABS sheets 2–3 were reread at full resolution from the repository. Read the two current-model views and owner south-gable sketch supplied in the follow-up to PR #243; inventory in docs/RESEARCH/glessner-south-gable/work.md. Five attachments read 2026-10-02: image.png (northwest archival-looking view, date not independently established); image(2).png (owner-directed reconstructed west elevation); image(3).png and image(4).png (north/west model defects); Untitled.png (turret alignment correction). These are compared as architecture, not reused as texture pixels. Four attachments viewed 8 October 2026 UTC (7 October owner local time): image(20261008-050643).png and image(20261008-050730).png (model defects), Pasted Graphic 31.png (aerial), and image(7).png (Tommy Henry, March 2023 courtyard roof detail). Three attachments viewed 8 October: image(20261008-090301).png (modern courtyard tower photograph), image(9).png and image(10).png (current application). HABS photograph 5 was reread to retain its divided sash. Two attachments viewed 9 October 2026 UTC: a 1196x864 historic-looking northwest view and a 1047x717 isolated west elevation study. Neither capture date nor the elevation study's rectification is independently established. They bound the requested reconstructed silhouette; no image pixels are republished or used as textures. Later 9 October 2026 UTC: the owner supplied a courtyard application screenshot (890x762) showing the missing roof and reaffirmed the earlier connected-roof diagrams. All three images in this exchange, the prior connected-roof plan and courtyard renders, and HABS photograph 05 were visually compared. The explicit level-ridge instruction supersedes the lower-ridge interpretation of the isolated west elevation study; that study constrains the west cross-gable/wall profile, not the entire roof volume.
note: A production brief, not historical testimony. It authorizes a reconstructed treatment of missing details but does not document their 1904 dimensions. The modern reference views explicitly influence reconstructed arrangements and material boundaries where identified in the dossier; this is acknowledged, not disguised as a HABS measurement.
what_it_supplies: The owner-requested visible omissions to correct in version 4.
Qualitative cross-check that a cross gable, west-wing courtyard windows, garden-level lights and a continuous corner copper roof should not be omitted.
T-1830 owner request and qualitative roof/entrance comparisons; first- and second-floor HABS plans supply dimensional control.
T-1833 owner-directed south-gable and matching courtyard-eave reconstruction, superseding the prior rear hip.
T-1999 controlling west-elevation reconstruction and explicit turret alignment; supersedes conflicting T-1833 rear-roof height assumptions.
T-2157 courtyard dining-roof reconstruction: forward copper hip, raised tiled connector, continuous host eave and matching crest.
what_it_does_not_supply: A measured survey or a dated 1904 view.
Reusable photographic textures or permission to redistribute third-party reference images.
Exact dimensions, colour, roof patina, plantings, or a pre-1946 date for an otherwise undocumented opening.
